post.description:
Creates a procedural media file — a background, texture, pattern, test card or countdown drawn by the engine itself (no stock footage, nothing downloaded) — and adds it to the project as a normal material, like CapCut's generated/stock backgrounds but fully original and offline. Still kinds (solid colours, still gradients, grids, checkers, stripes, textures, patterns, colour bars without tone) are written as a PNG (material type photo, duration 0: it can be stretched to any length on the timeline); banner and frame are PNGs with a transparent background meant for an overlay track; kinds that move (speed > 0, noise, countdowns, timers) or make sound (colour-bar tone, countdown beeps) are rendered frame by frame and encoded to an H.264 MP4 of duration_us (material type video). Files go to <project>/cache/generated/ and are reused when the same kind, params, size, duration and fps are asked again (cached = true; the existing material is returned instead of a duplicate). Pick a ready-made look with preset_id (ids from library.list kind=generated, e.g. "sunset_gradient", "neon_floor", "countdown_5", "film_grain") — params then override single preset values — or give kind + params yourself. Size defaults to the project canvas; videos use the canvas fps (or 30) and even pixel sizes. With add_to_timeline the new material is also placed in the same undo step, exactly like timeline.segment.add: on the main track at the clip boundary nearest at_us (magnet), or appended to the end of the main track when at_us is omitted; track_id / new_track choose another track (e.g. an overlay track for grain, confetti, light leaks, film dust, banners or frames on top of a clip — light_leak and film_dust are drawn on black for segment.set_blend mode screen). Moving backgrounds with a loop param (mesh, aurora, lava, plasma, bokeh, particles, light_leak) repeat seamlessly every loop seconds, which is also their default length. Rendering runs while the command executes (typically 2-10 s for 5 s of 1080p video); duration_us is limited to 60 s — for longer backgrounds use a still kind or add the clip several times. Undo removes the material (and the placed clip); the cached file stays on disk. Kinds: • solid — a flat colour card (PNG) — backgrounds, chroma-key plates, fade cards. Params: color (color, default "#000000"): Fill colour.. • gradient — a smooth linear or radial colour gradient (PNG, or a flowing video when speed > 0). Params: colors (colors, 2-6, default ["#FF7A59","#7B2FF7"]): Colour stops, evenly spaced, from start to end (2-6).; type (enum linear|radial, default "linear"): linear = along angle; radial = from the centre outwards.; angle (number -360..360, default 135): Direction of a linear gradient in degrees: 0 = left to right, 90 = top to bottom.; speed (number 0..5, default 0): Colour flow speed in back-and-forth cycles per 10 seconds. 0 = a still picture (PNG).. • color_bars — a test card of vertical colour bars (PNG, or a video with a sine tone when tone = true). Params: style (enum classic|rainbow|retro, default "classic"): classic = broadcast-style 75% bars with a lower calibration row; rainbow = 12 hues over a grey step wedge; retro = muted 70s palette.; tone (boolean, default false): Add a continuous sine test tone (the output becomes a video with sound).; tone_hz (number 100..8000, default 1000): Frequency of the test tone in hertz.. • noise — film grain, TV static, paper and soft cloudy textures from value noise (video while speed > 0, else PNG). Params: color (color, default "#808080"): Base colour; the noise brightens and darkens it.; color2 (color): Optional second colour: the noise blends between color and color2 instead of brightening/darkening.; amount (number 0..1, default 0.5): Strength (contrast) of the noise.; scale (number 1..400, default 1): Grain size in pixels at 1080p height: 1-2 = fine grain/static, 100+ = soft clouds.; octaves (integer 1..5, default 1): Layers of finer detail added on top (fractal noise); 3-4 for paper and smoke.; monochrome (boolean, default true): Same noise in R, G and B (false = coloured RGB noise).; speed (number 0..4, default 1): How fast the noise changes: 1 = 24 new grain patterns per second (soft noise drifts smoothly). 0 = a still picture (PNG).; seed (integer 0..1e+06, default 1): Random seed: another number gives another pattern.. • shapes — circles, rounded squares, triangles and rings drifting over a colour (video while speed > 0, else PNG). Params: shape (enum mixed|circle|square|triangle|ring, default "mixed"): Which shapes to draw.; count (integer 1..80, default 18): Number of shapes.; colors (colors, 1-8, default ["#FF5C8A","#FFD23F","#3EC1D3","#9B5DE5","#00F5D4"]): Shape colours, used in turn.; background (color, default "#16161D"): Background colour.; size (number 0.01..0.5, default 0.07): Average shape radius as a fraction of the frame height.; opacity (number 0.1..1, default 0.9): Shape opacity.; speed (number 0..5, default 1): Drift speed (1 = calm). 0 = a still picture (PNG).; seed (integer 0..1e+06, default 7): Random seed for positions, sizes and directions.. • countdown — a numeric countdown (from N to 1, one number per second by default) as a video. Params: from (integer 1..60, default 5): First number; the clip counts down to 1. Default length = from seconds.; style (enum ring|plain|film, default "ring"): ring = number inside an emptying progress ring; plain = big fading numbers; film = projector-leader look with a sweeping wedge and crosshair (use a light background).; background (color, default "#111114"): Background colour.; color (color, default "#FFFFFF"): Colour of the numbers (and of the film-style circles).; accent (color, default "#FF3B5C"): Colour of the progress ring / sweeping wedge.; beep (boolean, default false): Add a short beep at every number (the video gets a sound track).. • grid — a line grid — flat (blueprint, graph paper) or a perspective floor running to the horizon (video while speed > 0, else PNG). Params: style (enum flat|perspective, default "flat"): flat = square grid; perspective = floor grid towards a horizon with a sky above.; color (color, default "#FFFFFF"): Line colour.; background (color, default "#101018"): Background (floor) colour.; color2 (color): Sky colour at the top of a perspective grid (default: the background colour).; cells (integer 2..64, default 12): Number of grid cells across the frame width.; thickness (number 0.5..20, default 2): Line thickness in pixels at 1080p height.; glow (boolean, default false): Soft neon glow around the lines (and on the horizon).; speed (number 0..5, default 0): Scroll speed in cells per second (towards the viewer). 0 = a still picture (PNG).. • checker — a two-colour checkerboard, optionally rotated and scrolling (video while speed > 0, else PNG). Params: color (color, default "#FFFFFF"): First square colour.; color2 (color, default "#D9D9E0"): Second square colour.; cells (integer 2..128, default 8): Number of squares across the frame width.; angle (number -180..180, default 0): Rotation of the pattern in degrees.; speed (number 0..5, default 0): Diagonal scroll speed in squares per second. 0 = a still picture (PNG).. • stripes — diagonal or straight stripes in 2-6 colours, optionally moving like a barber pole (video while speed > 0, else PNG). Params: colors (colors, 2-6, default ["#FFD23F","#1B1B1F"]): Stripe colours, repeated in order.; width (number 0.005..0.5, default 0.06): Width of one stripe as a fraction of the frame height.; angle (number -180..180, default 45): Stripe direction in degrees: 0 = vertical stripes, 90 = horizontal.; speed (number 0..10, default 0): Movement in stripes per second. 0 = a still picture (PNG).. • mesh — a soft modern mesh gradient: colour clouds blended into each other, slowly drifting in a seamless loop (video while speed > 0, else PNG). Params: colors (colors, 2-6, default ["#FF9A8B","#FF6A88","#FF99AC","#FAD0C4","#A18CD1"]): Colours of the blended clouds (2-6).; softness (number 0..1, default 0.5): 0 = distinct colour patches, 1 = very soft, misty blending.; grain (number 0..0.3, default 0.04): Fine film grain on top (0 = clean).; speed (number 0..3, default 1): How far the colour clouds drift (1 = calm). 0 = a still picture (PNG).; loop (number 2..30, default 8): Seconds until the motion repeats exactly (seamless loop); also the default clip length.; seed (integer 0..1e+06, default 3): Random seed: another number gives another arrangement.. • aurora — northern lights: glowing curtains of light waving over a starry night sky (video while speed > 0, else PNG). Params: colors (colors, 2-4, default ["#00FFA3","#00C2FF","#B026FF"]): Curtain colours from the bottom edge of the light upwards.; background (color, default "#040714"): Night sky colour at the top.; color2 (color, default "#0A2A3C"): Sky colour near the horizon (bottom).; stars (boolean, default true): Twinkling stars in the sky.; landscape (boolean, default true): Dark mountain and forest silhouette along the bottom.; speed (number 0..3, default 1): Wave speed of the curtains. 0 = a still picture (PNG).; loop (number 2..30, default 10): Seconds until the motion repeats exactly (seamless loop); also the default clip length.; seed (integer 0..1e+06, default 5): Random seed: another number gives another arrangement.. • lava — glossy blobs that rise, sink, merge and split like a lava lamp (video while speed > 0, else PNG). Params: colors (colors, 1-4, default ["#FFB000","#FF3D6E","#B5179E"]): Blob colours from top to bottom of the frame.; background (color, default "#1B0B2E"): Background colour at the top.; color2 (color, default "#3A0D4F"): Background colour at the bottom.; count (integer 2..16, default 7): Number of blobs.; size (number 0.04..0.3, default 0.13): Blob radius as a fraction of the frame height.; speed (number 0..3, default 1): Rise/sink speed. 0 = a still picture (PNG).; loop (number 2..30, default 10): Seconds until the motion repeats exactly (seamless loop); also the default clip length.; seed (integer 0..1e+06, default 11): Random seed: another number gives another arrangement.. • plasma — a retro demo-scene plasma: interfering colour waves cycling through a palette (video while speed > 0, else PNG). Params: colors (colors, 2-6, default ["#120458","#7A04EB","#FF00A0","#FE75FE","#00F0FF"]): Palette the waves cycle through.; scale (number 0.3..6, default 1.5): Wave density: higher = more, smaller ripples.; speed (number 0..3, default 1): Wave speed. 0 = a still picture (PNG).; loop (number 2..30, default 8): Seconds until the motion repeats exactly (seamless loop); also the default clip length.; seed (integer 0..1e+06, default 2): Random seed: another number gives another arrangement.. • bokeh — out-of-focus light discs drifting and twinkling over a dark gradient, like city lights behind a lens (video while speed > 0, else PNG). Params: colors (colors, 1-6, default ["#FFD27A","#FF9F5A","#FFF2C4"]): Light colours.; background (color, default "#120E1C"): Background colour at the top.; color2 (color, default "#2B1B2E"): Background colour at the bottom.; count (integer 4..150, default 36): Number of light discs.; size (number 0.01..0.3, default 0.08): Average disc radius as a fraction of the frame height.; softness (number 0..1, default 0.35): Edge softness: 0 = crisp discs, 1 = very blurry.; speed (number 0..3, default 1): Drift speed. 0 = a still picture (PNG).; loop (number 2..30, default 10): Seconds until the motion repeats exactly (seamless loop); also the default clip length.; seed (integer 0..1e+06, default 8): Random seed: another number gives another arrangement.. • particles — light particles: floating dust, fireflies, falling snow, twinkling stars or rising embers (video while speed > 0, else PNG). Params: style (enum dust|fireflies|snow|stars|embers, default "dust"): dust = slow glowing motes; fireflies = wandering pulsing green-gold lights; snow = flakes falling with a sway; stars = twinkling starfield; embers = sparks rising and flickering.; color (color, default "#FFFFFF"): Particle colour (fireflies and embers tint it warmer).; background (color, default "#0B0F1A"): Background colour at the top.; color2 (color): Optional background colour at the bottom (vertical gradient).; count (integer 10..800, default 160): Number of particles.; size (number 0.2..5, default 1): Particle size multiplier.; speed (number 0..3, default 1): Movement speed. 0 = a still picture (PNG).; loop (number 2..30, default 8): Seconds until the motion repeats exactly (seamless loop); also the default clip length.; seed (integer 0..1e+06, default 4): Random seed: another number gives another arrangement.. • light_leak — film light leaks, burns, prism streaks and lens flares on black — put it on an overlay track with the Screen (or Add) blend mode (video while speed > 0, else PNG). Params: style (enum leak|burn|prism|flare, default "leak"): leak = soft warm glows drifting in from the edges; burn = hot film burn flaring from one side; prism = rainbow streaks sweeping across; flare = lens flare with a moving source, streak and ghost rings.; colors (colors, 1-5, default ["#FF3D00","#FF8A00","#FFC14D"]): Light colours (prism uses a rainbow when only defaults are given).; intensity (number 0.2..1.5, default 1): Brightness of the light.; speed (number 0..3, default 1): Movement speed. 0 = a still picture (PNG).; loop (number 2..30, default 6): Seconds until the motion repeats exactly (seamless loop); also the default clip length.; seed (integer 0..1e+06, default 9): Random seed: another number gives another arrangement.. • film_dust — old-film dirt on black: dust specks, hairs and vertical scratches flickering every frame — use the Screen blend mode on top of a clip (video while speed > 0, else PNG). Params: color (color, default "#FFFFFF"): Colour of the dirt.; amount (number 0..1, default 0.5): How much dirt.; speed (number 0..2, default 1): 1 = new dirt 12 times per second, like a projector. 0 = a still picture (PNG).; seed (integer 0..1e+06, default 6): Random seed: another number gives another arrangement.. • texture — a still material texture: paper, kraft paper, grunge wall, concrete, canvas, denim, marble, watercolour paper or wood (PNG). Params: style (enum paper|kraft|grunge|concrete|canvas|denim|marble|watercolor|wood, default "paper"): Material to imitate.; color (color): Base colour (default depends on the style).; color2 (color): Accent colour: fibres, stains, veins, watercolour blooms or grain (default depends on the style).; amount (number 0..1, default 0.5): Strength of the texture detail.; scale (number 0.25..4, default 1): Size of the texture features.; seed (integer 0..1e+06, default 7): Random seed: another number gives another arrangement.. • pattern — a decorative repeating pattern — memphis, waves, polka dots, halftone, terrazzo, chevron, honeycomb, gingham, scales, dot grid, isometric cubes or triangle mosaic (PNG, or a slowly scrolling video when speed > 0). Params: style (enum memphis|waves|dots|halftone|terrazzo|chevron|honeycomb|gingham|scales|dot_grid|cubes|triangles, default "memphis"): Pattern design.; colors (colors, 2-6, default ["#FFF4E6","#FF6B6B","#4ECDC4","#FFD93D","#6A4C93"]): Background colour first, then the pattern colours.; scale (number 2..64, default 8): Pattern repeats across the frame width.; angle (number -180..180, default 0): Rotation of the pattern in degrees.; speed (number 0..5, default 0): Diagonal scroll speed in repeats per second. 0 = a still picture (PNG).; seed (integer 0..1e+06, default 12): Random seed: another number gives another arrangement.. • timer — a styled countdown video from N to 1 — flip clock, neon ring, progress bar, vanishing dots or pop-art bursts. Params: from (integer 1..60, default 5): First number; the clip counts down to 1. Default length = from seconds.; style (enum flip|neon|bar|dots|pop, default "flip"): flip = split-flap clock cards that flip every second; neon = glowing ring and digits; bar = big number over a shrinking progress bar; dots = a ring of dots that go out one by one; pop = the number punches in over a coloured starburst.; background (color, default "#121216"): Background colour.; color (color, default "#FFFFFF"): Colour of the numbers.; accent (color, default "#FF3B5C"): Accent colour (cards, ring, bar, dots, bursts).; beep (boolean, default false): Add a short beep at every number (the video gets a sound track).. • banner — a text-free banner shape on a transparent background — lower third, pill, tab, ribbon, glass panel, news bar or brush stroke — to put your own text on (PNG with alpha). Params: style (enum lower_third|pill|tab|ribbon|glass|news|brush, default "lower_third"): Banner design.; color (color, default "#FFFFFF"): Main panel colour.; color2 (color, default "#FF3B5C"): Accent colour (bars, tags, ribbon ends, icon slot).; position (enum bottom|center|top, default "bottom"): Vertical position in the frame.; width (number 0.2..1, default 0.6): Banner width as a fraction of the frame width.. • frame — a border overlay with a transparent centre — film strip, neon, instant photo, vignette, torn paper, viewfinder, rounded, postage stamp or double line (PNG with alpha). Params: style (enum film|neon|polaroid|vignette|torn|viewfinder|rounded|stamp|double, default "rounded"): Frame design.; color (color, default "#FFFFFF"): Main frame colour (vignette: the shadow colour).; color2 (color, default "#FF3B5C"): Accent colour (neon glow, viewfinder REC dot, inner line).; thickness (number 0.01..0.25, default 0.05): Border thickness as a fraction of the frame height..
UI: Library/Stickers/Generated.
Undoable with edit.undo.

Returns one material with everything known about it: the probed metadata, whether the file is missing, every timeline segment that uses it (track, segment id, timeline and source ranges), which background assets are ready (thumbnail, waveform, filmstrip, proxy) and the URLs of its preview endpoints. post.description:
Imports video, photo and audio files into the project's media library — the Import button of the Media panel (left panel → Media → Local), the native file dialog, or dropping files onto the window. Every file is probed with ffprobe: type (video / photo / audio, detected from the streams and extension; animated GIFs are videos, single-frame GIFs are photos), duration (photos get 0 because they can be stretched to any length), display width/height (already swapped for 90°/270° rotated phone videos), rotation, frame rate, video/audio codecs, sample rate, channels and file size. A folder path imports the supported media files directly inside it (not recursive, max 500). Files already in the project (same path) are not imported twice: they are reported in duplicates with their existing material_id. Files that cannot be imported (missing, relative path, not a media file) are reported in errors without failing the whole import; the command only fails when nothing at all could be imported. Importing does NOT place anything on the timeline — call timeline.segment.add with the returned material ids for that. After the command returns, thumbnails, the filmstrip and audio waveforms are generated in the background: watch the media.import.progress events and media.ready (data.stage = "assets") on the event stream; the thumbnail/frame/waveform endpoints also work immediately (they generate on demand).
UI: Library/Media/Import. Hotkey: Ctrl+I.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {materials: [Material], duplicates: [{path, material_id}], errors: [{path, code, message}]}. Material = {id, type (video|photo|audio), name, path, duration_us, width, height, rotation, fps, video_codec, has_audio, audio_codec, sample_rate, channels, size_bytes, imported_at}.

Pauses playback, leaving the playhead where playback reached (pressing Pause under the player). Pausing when nothing is playing is harmless and just returns the current state. Publishes a playback.state event {playing:false, time_us} and moves the playhead (playhead.moved). Use playback.seek afterwards to put the playhead at an exact time.
UI: Player/Pause.
Returns: {playing, time_us, duration_us, fps}: time_us is the playhead after the command.

post.description:
Starts playback from the playhead (or from from_us), like pressing Play under the player. If the playhead is at the end of the timeline, playback starts over from 0. While playing, the engine advances the playhead about 10 times per second (playhead.moved events, source "playback") and stops by itself at the end; the editor shows the composited stream (/stream) with sound (/audio). Publishes a playback.state event {playing, time_us}. Playing an empty timeline does nothing and returns playing=false. Playback state is not saved in the project and is not undoable.
UI: Player/Play.
Returns: {playing, time_us, duration_us, fps}: time_us is the playhead after the command.

post.description:
Moves the playhead to time_us — clicking or dragging on the timeline ruler. The player then shows the frame at that time (render it yourself with preview.frame). If playback is running it continues from the new position (a playback.state event with the new time_us is published). Publishes playhead.moved.

Returns: {playing, time_us, duration_us, fps}: time_us is the playhead after the command.

When starting, playback begins at the playhead (from 0 if the playhead is at the end) and the engine advances the playhead in real time until the end of the timeline. When pausing, the playhead stays where playback reached. Publishes playback.state {playing, time_us}; every connected editor and API client sees the change.
UI: Player/Play button. Hotkey: Space.
Returns: {playing, time_us, duration_us, fps}: time_us is the playhead after the command.

post.description:
Applies a preset from the user's kit to a clip, like clicking a card in "My kit" with a clip selected. Only the part stored in the preset changes (e.g. a filter preset sets only the filter). This is one undo step. Clips on locked tracks are rejected (conflict); a preset of the wrong kind for the clip fails with invalid_argument and a hint. Kinds and their targets: text_style → text clips (content, word timings and animations of the target are kept); adjust → video, photo and adjustment clips; filter → video, photo, sticker and filter clips; effect → video, photo and sticker clips (merged into the clip's effect list, same id replaced) or effect clips (first effect); transition → the LEFT clip of two touching clips on a video track (duration clamped to half of the shorter clip); animation → video, photo, sticker and text clips (In/Out replace Combo and vice versa, durations fit into the clip; loop and per-letter parts only for text).

Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {preset_id, kind, name, segment_id, segment: the updated segment, notes: adjustments made to fit the clip (e.g. a clamped transition duration)}.

Fails with invalid_argument when the clip has nothing of that kind (e.g. no filter). The project is not modified, so this is not an undo step. Re-apply with presets.apply. Kinds and their targets: text_style → text clips (content, word timings and animations of the target are kept); adjust → video, photo and adjustment clips; filter → video, photo, sticker and filter clips; effect → video, photo and sticker clips (merged into the clip's effect list, same id replaced) or effect clips (first effect); transition → the LEFT clip of two touching clips on a video track (duration clamped to half of the shorter clip); animation → video, photo, sticker and text clips (In/Out replace Combo and vice versa, durations fit into the clip; loop and per-letter parts only for text).

post.description:
Renders several evenly spaced frames of the project into one PNG grid (a contact sheet) so an AI agent can review the whole edit — pacing, cuts, text and overlays — in a single image instead of calling preview.frame many times. Frames are sampled at the centre of `count` equal slices of [start_us, end_us) (default: the whole timeline) and laid out left-to-right, top-to-bottom; times_us lists the time of each tile in that order. Uses the same renderer as the player and export. Read-only.

Returns: {width, height, columns, rows, tile_width, tile_height, times_us[], png_base64, warnings?}.

post.description:
Renders the composited picture of the project at one timeline time — exactly what the player shows and what export will contain, because the same renderer is used: every visible track in order (main video, overlays, stickers, text, then filter/effect/adjustment tracks applied to everything below them), transforms, crop, opacity, blend modes, masks, chroma key, filters, adjustments, effects, animations, keyframes and transitions. Use it after edits to SEE the result. Returns the frame as base64 PNG plus `url`, the binary endpoint GET /api/v1/projects/{id}/frame (add the API token as Authorization header or ?token=; supports &w=, &h= and &format=png|jpeg). time_us defaults to the playhead; times past the end show only the canvas background. The height follows the canvas aspect ratio. Missing or undecodable media is skipped and listed in `warnings`. Read-only: the project and playhead are not changed.
UI: Player.
Returns: {width, height, time_us, png_base64, url, warnings?, note}: png_base64 is the PNG file encoded as base64; url is the path of the same frame on the /frame endpoint (JPEG by default).

post.description:
Returns where every visible clip is drawn on the canvas at one moment — the boxes the player uses for on-canvas selection, move/scale/rotate handles and snapping, and that agents can use to reason about composition (e.g. 'is the title over the face?'). Covers video, photo, sticker and text segments of visible tracks (effects, filters, adjustments and audio have no box). Coordinates are canvas pixels of Project.Canvas (e.g. 1920x1080), origin top-left, +y down. Each box gives the unrotated rectangle x, y, w, h, its centre cx, cy, rotation in degrees clockwise around the centre and the four rotated corners; w/h include crop, fit, transform.scale, keyframes and the current In/Out/Combo animation (exactly the renderer's placement); text boxes are the rendered text image (incl. stroke, shadow, box). transform holds the keyframed values without animation (what segment.set_transform edits) and base_w/base_h the size at scale 1, so a handle drag maps back to x = transform.x + dx/(canvas_width/2), scale = new_w/base_w. Boxes are in compositing order: the LAST box is on top, so hit-test from the end. Both clips of a running transition are listed. Read-only.
UI: Player.
Returns: {time_us, canvas_width, canvas_height, boxes:[{segment_id, track_id, track_type, type: video|photo|sticker|text, x, y, w, h, rotation, cx, cy, corners:[[x,y]×4 TL,TR,BR,BL], flip_h?, flip_v?, opacity, z, locked?, animated?, base_w, base_h, transform:{x, y, scale, rotation}, missing?}], warnings?}.

The value is stored in project.cover_us (null = first frame) and is one undo step. Moving or trimming clips later does not move the cover time.

Resets one group of a segment's properties to CapCut's defaults — the ↺ buttons of the inspector sections. A specific group that does not apply (e.g. audio on a photo) is rejected with invalid_argument. Content (text, source range, filters, effects, transitions) is never touched.

Sets colour/light controls of a video or photo clip, or of an adjustment segment (which applies to all tracks below it) — the Adjustment tab → Basic in CapCut. Omitted fields keep their value. Fields animated by keyframes (adjust.<field>) record the value as a keyframe at the playhead. Render order: exposure → brightness → contrast → highlights/shadows → temperature/tint → hue + HSL → saturation → curves → fade → LUT → shine → sharpen → vignette → grain. Per-colour-range changes use segment.set_hsl, tone curves segment.set_curves, automatic correction adjustment.auto_enhance; segment.reset_adjust returns everything (incl. HSL and curves) to neutral.

Undoable with edit.undo.

post.description:
Sets the tone curves of a video/photo clip or adjustment segment — the Curves page of CapCut's Adjustment tab. A curve maps input level x to output level y (both 0..1, 0 = black, 1 = white) through up to 16 control points joined by a smooth monotone cubic (no overshoot: rising points give a rising curve). The master (luma) curve applies to all channels first, then the r, g and b curves. Ways to call it: preset alone replaces every channel with a built-in look (lighten, darken, fade, contrast, cool, warm, vintage; custom = straight lines to edit by hand); channel + points replaces one channel (channel defaults to master); preset + channel + points starts from the preset and then replaces that channel. points is an array of [x, y] pairs or {x, y} objects; they are sorted by x, x values must differ, and the straight line [[0,0],[1,1]] means 'no change'. Examples of shapes: S-curve [[0,0],[0.25,0.18],[0.75,0.82],[1,1]] adds contrast; [[0,0.1],[1,1]] lifts the blacks (matte); a red curve [[0,0],[0.5,0.56],[1,1]] warms the midtones. Curves render after the basic sliders and HSL and before a .cube LUT.
UI: Inspector/Adjustment/Curves.
Undoable with edit.undo.

post.description:
Adjusts one colour range of a video/photo clip or adjustment segment — the HSL page of CapCut's Adjustment tab (8 colour dots). Bands: red (0°), orange (30°), yellow (60°), green (120°), cyan (180°), blue (240°), purple (270°), magenta (300°). Each band has h (hue shift: -1 = -30° … +1 = +30° around the colour wheel), s (saturation: -1 = grey, +1 = double) and l (lightness: -1 darker … +1 lighter), all -1..1 with 0 = unchanged. Pixels between two band centres belong to both with smooth weights, so there are no hard edges, and a band never affects hues beyond its neighbours (shifting red does not touch blue). Neutral greys are never changed. Omitted h/s/l keep their value. band "all" writes the given values into every band (e.g. s -1 → black and white). Alternatively pass bands = {red: {h, s, l}, …} to set several bands at once (omitted bands and fields are kept). Use segment.reset_hsl to clear one band or all of them. Typical recipes: bluer sky = blue {s: 0.3, l: -0.2}; greener foliage = yellow {h: 0.4} + green {s: 0.3}; skin = orange {s: -0.1, l: 0.1}.
UI: Inspector/Adjustment/HSL.
Undoable with edit.undo.

These play INSIDE the text image and combine freely with each other and with the clip-level animations of animation.set. kind=in plays over duration_us from the segment start, kind=out over duration_us up to the segment end (in and out are shortened proportionally when they do not both fit), kind=loop repeats with duration_us as the period for the whole segment. A bare name is qualified with kind ("typewriter" + in → "in_typewriter"). Without duration_us the slot keeps its current duration, else the item's default_duration_us is used; in/out durations are clamped to the segment length.
UI: Inspector/Text/Animate.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: The updated TextStyle (glyph_in / glyph_out / glyph_loop = {id, duration_us}).

post.description:
Changes the content and look of a text segment — the Text tab of the inspector (Basic: font, size, style, colour, case, alignment, spacing; Stroke; Extra outlines; Shadow; Background box; Glow; Gradient fill; 3D extrude; Curve; Word-art effect; caption highlight). Only the parameters you pass change. Units: size is CapCut's scale (15 = default, font height ≈ size/300 of the canvas height); letter_spacing and line_spacing are in em (0.1 = 10% of the font size) added to the normal spacing; stroke_width, shadow_blur and shadow_distance are 0..1 (stroke up to 0.25 em thick, shadow offset/blur up to 0.5 em); shadow_angle, fill_angle and extrude_angle are in degrees counter-clockwise from the right (-45 = down-right, -90 = downwards / top→bottom); box_radius 0..1 rounds the corners (1 = pill). Stroke, shadow, box, glow and extrude are enabled by setting any of their parameters (missing ones get defaults: black stroke width 0.3, black shadow opacity 0.6/blur 0.3/distance 0.15/angle -45, black box opacity 0.6/radius 0.2, glow in the text colour intensity 0.6/radius 0.35, dark-grey extrude depth 0.15/angle -45) and removed with stroke_width=0, shadow_opacity=0, box_opacity=0, glow_intensity=0 or extrude_depth=0. Gradient fill: fill_type linear|radial with 2–4 fill_colors (evenly spaced; radial goes centre→edge), fill_type=solid removes it (the text colour is used again); passing only fill_colors turns on a linear gradient. A color with alpha 00 ("#FFFFFF00") plus a stroke gives hollow outline text. curve -1..1 bends the lines into an arc (1 = half circle arch, -1 = smile). case upper|lower|title converts letters when rendering (the stored content is unchanged; none = as typed). effect_id applies a word-art preset from library.list kind=text_effect FIRST (it writes fill, glow, extra_strokes, extrude and the stroke/shadow/color it uses — the rendered look comes only from the stored fields), so other parameters in the same call override it; effect_id "" or "none" removes the preset's fill/glow/extra outlines/extrusion. Captions: words (timings relative to the segment start) plus highlight_style color|box|scale|underline|karaoke|pop|bounce|reveal|dim|glow|sweep_line|slide_box highlight the spoken word (highlight_style=none removes it). Per-letter animations are set with text.set_glyph_animation. Wave-4 word art (all optional; each group is enabled by any of its parameters and removed by its zero amount): fill_stops (hard-edged chrome/duotone gradients, up to 8 fill_colors); stroke_fill_* (gradient outline); pattern_* (procedural texture over the fill: stripes, checker, dots, halftone, hearts, stars, grain, glitter, holo, foil, brushed metal, marble, camo, galaxy, lava flow, aurora, rainbow…, pattern_speed animates the moving ones); bevel_* (emboss lighting; bevel_round + bevel_gloss = puffy glossy letters); inner_shadow_* and inner_glow_* (inside the letters); echo_* (stacked offset copies, retro 3D stacks / trails); distress_* (grunge, chalk, stamp, spray, scratch, worn); sparkle_* (star glints, sparkle_speed twinkles); drip_* (paint or slime drips); rough (hand-made wobble); pixelate (pixel-art blocks); box_* extras (gradient box, border, card shadow, one box per line, skew, padding, knockout stencil); highlight_text_color (letter colour of the active caption word). Highlight styles also include pop, bounce, reveal, dim, glow, sweep_line and slide_box.
UI: Inspector/Text.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: The updated TextStyle object of the segment.

align.description: Horizontal alignment of lines within the text block.

bevel_angle.description: Direction the bevel light comes from, counter-clockwise from the right (135 = upper left, the default). Unit: degrees.

bevel_depth.description: Bevel / emboss lighting: width of the lit edge 0..1 (1 = 0.25 em); 0 removes the bevel.

bevel_gloss.description: Sharp specular highlight on the bevel (glossy plastic / puffy balloon look) 0..1.

bevel_highlight.description: Bevel light colour #RRGGBB (default white; gold-ish for warm metal).

bevel_round.description: Rounded pillow profile (puffy, inflated letters) instead of a flat chisel.

bevel_strength.description: Contrast of the bevel light and shade 0..1 (default 0.8).

bold.description: Bold style (a real bold face when the font has one, otherwise synthesised).

box_border_color.description: Colour #RRGGBB of an outline drawn inside the edge of the background box.

box_border_width.description: Box outline thickness 0..1 (1 = 0.25 em); 0 removes it.

box_color.description: Background box colour #RRGGBB. Enables the box if it was off.

box_fill_angle.description: Direction of the box gradient, counter-clockwise from the right. Unit: degrees.

box_fill_colors.description: 2–8 colours of a gradient background box (left→right unless box_fill_angle); [] removes the gradient. Enables the box if it was off.

box_knockout.description: Cut the letters out of the box so the video shows through them (stencil look).

box_opacity.description: Background box opacity 0..1; 0 removes the box.

box_pad.description: Extra padding around the text inside the box 0..1 (1 = 0.5 em).

box_per_line.description: One box per text line (ribbon / highlighter captions) instead of one box around the block.

box_radius.description: Corner roundness 0..1 (fraction of half the box height; 1 = pill).

box_shadow_angle.description: Box shadow direction, counter-clockwise from the right (-45 = down-right). Unit: degrees.

box_shadow_color.description: Colour #RRGGBB of a drop shadow under the background box (blur 0 = flat offset "card" shadow).

box_skew.description: Slants the box into a parallelogram (-1..1; positive leans right) — sports and news lower thirds.

case.description: Letter case conversion at render time: upper (ABC), lower (abc), title (Abc Def) or none (as typed).

color.description: Text colour as #RRGGBB (or #RRGGBBAA; alpha 00 + a stroke = hollow text).

content.description: New text content; \n starts a new line. Must not be empty.

curve.description: Arc bend of every line: 0 = straight, 1 = half-circle arch (∩), -1 = half-circle smile (∪).

distress_amount.description: How much is eroded 0..1; 0 removes the distress.

distress_type.description: Erodes the whole text with a texture: grunge (rough print), chalk (chalkboard), stamp (rubber stamp), spray (speckled spray paint), scratch (scratched lines), worn (faded vintage print); none removes it.

drip_amount.description: Paint / slime drips hanging from the letters 0..1 (horror, slime, melting looks); 0 removes them.

echo_angle.description: Direction of the echo copies, counter-clockwise from the right (-45 = down-right). Unit: degrees.

echo_colors.description: Echo: 1–6 colours #RRGGBB(AA) of offset copies of the letters stacked behind the text, nearest first (retro 70s/80s stacks, motion trails with fading alpha); [] removes the echo.

echo_distance.description: Distance between echo copies 0..1 (1 = 0.5 em); 0 removes the echo.

echo_hollow.description: Draw the echo copies as thin outlines instead of solid shapes.

effect_id.description: Word-art preset from library.list kind=text_effect (e.g. "fx_gold_metal", "fx_neon_outline"), applied before the other parameters; "" or "none" removes the preset's fill/glow/extra outlines/extrusion.

extra_strokes.description: Additional outlines OUTSIDE the main stroke, inner → outer, each {color:"#RRGGBB", width:0..1} (width like stroke_width); at most 4; [] removes them.

extrude_angle.description: Extrusion direction, counter-clockwise from the right: -45 = down-right (default), -90 = straight down. Unit: degrees.

extrude_color.description: 3D extrusion colour #RRGGBB (shaded darker with depth); #RRGGBBAA with alpha < FF draws a fading long shadow. Enables the extrusion if it was off.

extrude_depth.description: Extrusion depth 0..1 em; 0 removes it. Unit: em.

fill_angle.description: Direction of a linear gradient, counter-clockwise from the right: 0 = left→right, -90 = top→bottom, 90 = bottom→top. Unit: degrees.

fill_colors.description: 2–4 gradient colour stops #RRGGBB(AA), evenly spaced: first at the start (linear) or centre (radial), last at the end/edge.

fill_stops.description: Positions 0..1 of the fill_colors stops (one per colour, ascending; two equal neighbours make a hard edge such as a chrome horizon); [] = evenly spaced.

fill_type.description: Fill of the letters: solid (the text colour; removes a gradient), linear or radial gradient through fill_colors.

font.description: Font id from library.list kind=font (e.g. "go_sans", "go_mono", "sys_arial", or a downloaded font such as "montserrat" — install free fonts with font.catalog + font.install). Characters the font lacks (Cyrillic, CJK…) fall back to system fonts automatically.

glow_color.description: Glow (soft coloured halo) colour #RRGGBB. Enables the glow if it was off.

glow_intensity.description: How strong/opaque the glow is near the letters, 0..1; 0 removes the glow.

glow_radius.description: Glow size 0..1 (1 ≈ a halo reaching 1.3 em beyond the letters).

highlight_color.description: Highlight colour #RRGGBB (default #FFD600). Enables a color highlight if none was set.

highlight_scale.description: Growth of the active word for highlight_style=scale (default 1.15).

highlight_style.description: How the spoken word is highlighted when words are set: color (word turns highlight_color), box (rounded box behind it), scale (word grows), underline, karaoke (fills left→right as spoken), pop (springs up with an overshoot), bounce (hops once), reveal (later words hidden until spoken), dim (later words dimmed), glow (halo behind the word), sweep_line (underline grows while spoken), slide_box (box glides from word to word); none removes the highlight.

highlight_text_color.description: Colour #RRGGBB of the active word's letters for the box / slide_box / underline / sweep_line / glow highlight styles (e.g. black text on a yellow box); "" keeps the text colour.

inner_glow_color.description: Inner glow colour #RRGGBB: light seeping in from the letter edges (neon tube, lit-from-within). Enables it if it was off.

inner_glow_radius.description: How far the inner glow reaches into the letters 0..1 (1 = 0.3 em).

inner_shadow_angle.description: Inner shadow offset direction, counter-clockwise from the right (-60 = down, slightly right). Unit: degrees.

inner_shadow_color.description: Inner shadow colour #RRGGBB: a shadow cast INSIDE the letters (debossed / cut-out look). Enables it if it was off.

italic.description: Italic style (real italic face or a synthetic slant).

letter_spacing.description: Extra space between characters in em (0 = normal). Unit: em.

line_spacing.description: Extra space between lines in em (0 = normal, 0.5 = half a line more). Unit: em.

pattern_angle.description: Rotates the pattern from its default orientation. Unit: degrees.

pattern_colors.description: Pattern colours #RRGGBB(AA); their meaning depends on pattern_type (see its list); omitted = the type's defaults, "" = use the text fill.

pattern_opacity.description: How strongly the pattern covers the fill, 0..1 (0 = fully, same as 1).

pattern_scale.description: Pattern feature size multiplier (1 = default size relative to the font, 2 = twice as big; 0 = default).

pattern_speed.description: Animation speed of moving patterns (holo shimmer, glitter twinkle, flowing lava, rainbow sweep, scrolling stripes…), cycles per second; 0 = still.

pattern_type.description: Procedural texture painted over the letter fill: stripes (diagonal two-colour stripes (candy cane / barber pole); colors [stripe, gap] (gap defaults to the fill); speed scrolls them); pinstripe (thin vertical pinstripes over the fill; colors [line]); checker (checkerboard (racing flag); colors [a, b]); gingham (picnic gingham: translucent crossing bands, darker where they overlap; colors [band, background]); plaid (woven tartan with a twill texture; colors [main, dark band, secondary, thin accent]); dots (polka dots on a staggered grid; colors [dot, background]); halftone (comic halftone dots growing from the top to the bottom of the text; colors [dot] (default: a darker shade of the fill)); hearts (tiny repeating hearts (kawaii, love); colors [heart, background]); stars (tiny repeating five-point stars; colors [star, background]); grain (film grain / risograph noise that roughens flat colour; speed makes it flicker); static (black-and-white TV static noise; speed animates it); scanlines (dark horizontal CRT scanlines; speed rolls them); brushed (brushed-metal streaks along the pattern angle (shades the fill)); foil (crinkled metal foil facets of random brightness (gold leaf, tinsel); speed makes facets glint); carbon (woven carbon fibre; colors [dark, highlight]); glitter (glitter flakes of varying brightness with bright sparkles; colors [glitter] (default: the fill); speed twinkles); holo (holographic / iridescent pastel rainbow with a soft sheen; colors = palette (2–8); speed shimmers); rainbow (saturated rainbow bands; speed sweeps them across the letters); aurora (northern-lights curtains of green, teal and violet; colors = palette; speed drifts them); flow (flowing lava / fire plasma; colors = palette from dark to bright; speed makes it flow); galaxy (deep-space nebula with tiny stars; colors = palette; speed twinkles the stars); marble (polished marble with thin veins; colors [stone, vein] (stone defaults to the fill)); wood (wood grain rings; colors [light, dark]); camo (camouflage blobs in four colours; colors [1..4]); leopard (leopard rosettes; colors [fur, ring, spot centre] (fur defaults to the fill)); zebra (wavy zebra stripes; colors [stripe, background]); frost (frosted ice cracks and rime; colors [frost]); grid (glowing synthwave grid lines; colors [line]; speed scrolls the grid). none removes it.

pixelate.description: Blocky pixel-art rendering 0..1 (1 = 0.2 em pixels); 0 = smooth.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

rough.description: Hand-made wobble: shaky outlines and slightly tilted letters 0..1 (marker, crayon, doodle looks); 0 = clean.

segment_id.description: ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id.

shadow_angle.description: Shadow direction, counter-clockwise from the right: -45 = down-right, 90 = up. Unit: degrees.

stroke_color.description: Outline colour #RRGGBB. Enables the stroke if it was off.

stroke_fill_angle.description: Direction of a linear stroke gradient, counter-clockwise from the right (0 = left→right, -90 = top→bottom). Unit: degrees.

stroke_fill_colors.description: 2–8 colour stops #RRGGBB(AA) of the stroke gradient; passing them alone turns on a linear stroke gradient (and a stroke if there was none).

post.description:
Returns a compact view of the timeline made for AI agents — much smaller than project.get. Tracks are listed top-to-bottom exactly as the CapCut timeline shows them: text/sticker/effect/filter and overlay tracks first, then the main_video track, then audio tracks. Each track has its id, type, layer (its compositing index in project.tracks: 0 is drawn first, at the bottom), lock/hide/mute flags and its clips in time order. Each clip has id, kind (video, photo, audio, sticker, text, effect, filter, adjustment), label (file name, text content or effect/filter id), start_us, end_us, duration_us, the source range it uses, speed, volume (video/audio), link_group, transition_out, filter and effects. Also returns markers, the current playhead, the timeline settings and a compact list of materials with how often each is used. Call it before editing to find segment and track ids, and after editing to check the result.
UI: Timeline.
Returns: {project_id, name, duration_us, playhead_us, fps, settings, tracks: [{id, type, name?, layer, muted, locked, hidden, segments: [{id, kind, label, start_us, end_us, duration_us, material_id?, source_start_us, source_duration_us, speed, reverse?, still?, volume?, link_group?, transition_out?, filter?, effects?}]}], markers: [{id, time_us, label?, color?}], materials: [{id, type, name, duration_us, uses}]}.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

post.description:
Adds a marker on the timeline ruler at at_us (default: the playhead) — CapCut's marker button / M. Markers are labelled points used to remember spots (e.g. beats) and clip edges snap to them. If a marker already exists at exactly that time it is returned instead of adding a duplicate (its label/colour are updated when given).
UI: Toolbar/Marker. Hotkey: M.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: The marker {id, time_us, label?, color?}.

post.description:
Places an imported material (from media.import / media.list) on the timeline as a new clip — like pressing + on a media card or dragging it onto the timeline in CapCut. Where it goes: without track_id, video and photo clips go to the main track (created if needed); audio, sticker and other clips go to the first track of their type that is free at at_us, otherwise to a new track. On the main track with the magnet on (default) the clip is inserted at the clip boundary nearest to at_us and every later clip ripples right — there are never gaps; when at_us is omitted it is appended to the end of the main track. With the magnet off it lands at at_us and later clips are pushed right only if they would overlap. On other tracks the clip starts exactly at at_us (default: the playhead); if that spot on the requested track is taken, CapCut creates a new track directly above it and puts the clip there. new_track forces a brand-new track. Length: the whole material for video/audio (from source_start_us), 5 s for photos, 3 s for stickers; duration_us overrides it but cannot exceed the material for video/audio. Video clips keep their own sound until audio.extract. Locked tracks cannot receive clips (conflict).
UI: Library/Media/Card/+ (or drag to the timeline).
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {track_id, segment} — the track that received the clip and the full new segment (id, source and target ranges, defaults: speed 1, scale 1, opacity 1, volume 1).

post.description:
Crops a video or photo clip — the Crop button in the timeline toolbar, which opens CapCut's crop dialog with ratio presets. Rectangle fields are fractions of the source frame (x,y = top-left corner, w,h = size; omitted fields keep the current crop, or the full frame). ratio fits the rectangle to an aspect ratio of the source pixels: with no rectangle it picks the largest centred area of that ratio; with a rectangle it shrinks it around its centre to match. 'free' keeps the rectangle as given. Calling it with neither a rectangle nor a fixed ratio resets the crop to the full frame (CapCut's Reset). A legacy rect object {x,y,w,h} is also accepted.
UI: Toolbar/Crop.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {segment} with segment.crop set (omitted when the crop was reset).

post.description:
Deletes clips from the timeline (the media stays in the library). On the main track with the magnet on the following clips shift left to close the gap (ripple delete); on other tracks a gap remains. Linked clips (e.g. a video and its extracted audio) are deleted together when linkage is on. Tracks other than the main track that become empty are removed, as in CapCut. The transition into a deleted clip is removed. Clips on locked tracks cannot be deleted.
UI: Toolbar/Delete. Hotkey: Delete.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {deleted: [segment ids]} — every removed clip including linked ones.

post.description:
Removes the part of a clip to the left of at_us (default: the playhead) — CapCut's "Delete left" (Q). On the main track with the magnet on the remaining part stays where the clip started and everything after it moves left, so the frame that was under the playhead is now at the clip's start (playhead_us; the editor moves the playhead there). Elsewhere the clip now starts at at_us. Linked clips are trimmed the same way. Without segment_id the main-track clip under at_us is used. at_us must lie strictly inside the clip.
UI: Toolbar/Delete left. Hotkey: Q.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {track_id, segment, playhead_us} — the shortened clip and the time the frame that was under the playhead now sits at.

post.description:

The clip is split at at_us, a 3-second still image of that frame (a new segment with still: true, silent, keeping the clip's look: transform, crop, filters, adjustments, effects, mask) is inserted, and the rest of the clip plus everything after it on that track moves 3 s to the right (linked clips follow). Works on video clips only (not photos or freeze frames). Without segment_id the main-track clip under at_us is used.
UI: Toolbar/Freeze.
Undoable with edit.undo.

post.description:
Mirrors a visual segment — the Mirror button in the timeline toolbar. Each call toggles the flip, so calling it twice restores the original. axis=horizontal (default) flips left↔right (Transform.flip_h); vertical flips upside down (flip_v). Use segment.set_transform {flip_h} to set an explicit state instead of toggling.
UI: Toolbar/Mirror.
Undoable with edit.undo.

post.description:
Moves a clip to a new start time and/or another track — the same as dragging it in the CapCut timeline. On the main track with the magnet on, a move re-orders the clips: the clip is taken out (its gap closes) and re-inserted at the clip boundary nearest to start_us, so there are never gaps. On other tracks the clip starts exactly at start_us; if it would overlap another clip there, a new track is created directly above the destination track (below it for audio) and the clip goes there. Cross-track moves must respect the track type: video/photo between main_video and video_overlay tracks, audio between audio tracks, text/sticker/effect/filter only within their own type. Moving a clip off the main track closes its gap (magnet). Linked clips (link_group, e.g. video + extracted audio) move by the same amount when linkage is on; a linked clip on the magnet main track leads. Snapping (auto_snapping, 100 ms) aligns either edge with other clip edges, the playhead, markers or 0. Start times below 0 are clamped to 0. Clips on locked tracks, or a locked destination, give a conflict error. Tracks left empty by the move disappear.
UI: Timeline/Drag clip.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {track_id, segment} — where the clip ended up (start may differ from start_us because of the magnet or snapping).

Rotates a visual segment by 90° — the Rotate button in the timeline toolbar. Clockwise by default; the result is normalised into -360..360 so four clicks return to 0°. For arbitrary angles use segment.set_transform {rotation}. If rotation is keyframed, the new angle becomes a keyframe at the playhead.
UI: Toolbar/Rotate.
Undoable with edit.undo.

post.description:
Splits a clip into two at at_us (default: the playhead), exactly like CapCut's Split button / Ctrl+B. Both halves keep every property (transform, filters, effects, adjustments, volume, speed, mask…); the left half keeps the original id and the in-animation and fade-in, the right half gets a new id, the out-animation, fade-out and the transition to the next clip. Keyframes are divided at the cut with an interpolated keyframe on both sides so the motion does not change. Linked clips that span the same time are split too and the right halves stay linked to each other. Without segment_id the main-track clip under at_us is split. at_us must lie strictly inside the clip.
UI: Toolbar/Split. Hotkey: Ctrl+B.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {track_id, left, right, linked_right_ids?} — both halves (full segments) and the ids of linked right halves.

post.description:
Moves the left or right edge of a clip to to_us — like dragging a clip edge in CapCut — which changes which part of the source is used. Video and audio cannot be extended past the start or end of their media (the edge stops there); photos, freeze frames, text, stickers, effects and filters can be stretched freely. Speed is respected: at 2x one second on the timeline uses two seconds of source (source_duration = duration × speed). A clip is never shorter than one frame. On the main track with the magnet on, the clip keeps its start and every later clip ripples (trimming the left edge removes content from the beginning and pulls the rest left); elsewhere the edge cannot pass the neighbouring clip. Linked clips are trimmed by the same amount. Keyframes stay attached to the content, fades and animations are shortened if needed, and a transition is shortened to at most half of either neighbour. If the request was limited, clamped is true and the segment shows the actual result.
UI: Timeline/Drag clip edge.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {track_id, segment, clamped} — the trimmed clip and whether the edge was limited by the media length, a neighbour or the minimum length.

post.description:
Stops a running tools.install_ffmpeg download (the Cancel button under the progress bar). The partial file is deleted and the job ends in state "cancelled"; FFmpeg stays missing until tools.install_ffmpeg is called again. Does nothing (cancelled=false) when no download is running.
UI: First run/Cancel.
Returns: {cancelled: true when a running download was stopped}.

Downloads FFmpeg for Kadr — the first-run "Download now" button. Fetches the BtbN GPL build of FFmpeg 7.1 for Windows x64 (about 100 MB) from GitHub, verifies its SHA-256 against the checksums.sha256 file of the same release (a mismatch deletes the download and fails), then extracts ONLY ffmpeg.exe and ffprobe.exe into %LOCALAPPDATA%\Kadr\tools\ffmpeg\bin where Kadr finds them immediately (no restart). Runs in the background and returns at once unless wait=true; progress arrives as tools.progress events (state downloading → verifying → extracting → done | failed | cancelled), or poll tools.status; stop it with tools.cancel. When FFmpeg is already available (PATH, next to Kadr, chosen folder) nothing is downloaded and already_installed=true, unless force=true. FFmpeg is licensed under the GPL (https://ffmpeg.org/legal.html). Only supported on Windows x64 (not_available elsewhere).
UI: First run/Download FFmpeg.
Returns: {started, already_installed, message, ...tools.status fields}.

force.description: Download Kadr's own copy even when an FFmpeg is already found (e.g. a broken or very old one on PATH).

source.description: Download source. Only "btbn" (github.com/BtbN/FFmpeg-Builds, GPL build, FFmpeg 7.1 branch) is available.

wait.description: Block until the download is verified and installed (can take minutes) instead of returning immediately.

post.description:
Points Kadr at an FFmpeg that is already on this computer — "I have FFmpeg — choose folder". The folder (or its bin subfolder) must contain both ffmpeg.exe and ffprobe.exe and ffmpeg must run ("-version"); it is saved as ffmpeg_dir in settings.json, used from now on (no restart) and on every start, and takes precedence over the copy next to Kadr, the downloaded copy and PATH. clear=true forgets the folder.
UI: First run/I have FFmpeg.
Returns: The tools.status object after the change.

clear.description: Forget the chosen folder and go back to automatic lookup.

dir.description: Absolute folder path, e.g. "C:\\ffmpeg\\bin" or "C:\\ffmpeg" (its bin subfolder is checked too). Required unless clear is true.

post.description:
Reports whether FFmpeg and FFprobe — required for importing, previewing and exporting media — are available, where they were found (source: env = KADR_FFMPEG, custom_dir = folder chosen with tools.set_ffmpeg_dir, next_to_exe, downloaded = Kadr's tools folder, path = system PATH) and their version, plus the state of a running tools.install_ffmpeg download and where it would download from (source, license, approximate size). Kadr does not bundle FFmpeg; when ffmpeg.found is false call tools.install_ffmpeg (Windows x64) or tools.set_ffmpeg_dir.
UI: Settings/FFmpeg.

post.description:
Finds a phrase in the transcript and cuts it out of the video — the easiest transcript edit for an AI agent ("delete 'so basically what I mean is'"). Matching ignores case and punctuation and is word by word within one clip. By default the first occurrence on the timeline is deleted (or the occurrence-th); all=true deletes every occurrence. The cut works like transcript.delete_words (split, delete, ripple, captions follow). One undo step; not_found when the phrase is not in the transcript.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {matches: total found, cuts: [{segment_id, start_us, end_us, text}], removed_us, captions_changed, duration_us}.

all.description: Delete every occurrence instead of one.

occurrence.description: Which occurrence to delete when all=false (1 = the first on the timeline).

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

ripple_captions.description: Make caption cues follow the cut (later cues move left, removed words disappear from their cue). Default true.

segment_id.description: Only search this clip (default: every transcribed audible clip).

text.description: The words to delete, e.g. "you know what I mean".

post.description:
Transcript-based editing: deletes words from a clip by cutting the video/audio where they are spoken (select words in the transcript → Delete). ranges are inclusive word indices from transcript.get for that segment_id. Each range removes the time from the first word's start to the last word's end plus the silence after it (up to 0.5 s, so the next word follows naturally): the clip is split, the part is deleted together with linked clips (extracted audio), and the rest of the track moves left (on the magnet main track every later clip ripples, and linked clips follow). Caption cues follow the cut unless ripple_captions=false. Everything is ONE undo step. Word indices of the clip change after the edit — call transcript.get again.
UI: Library/Transcript/Delete.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {cuts: [{segment_id, start_us, end_us, text}] (timeline times before the edit), removed_us, captions_changed, duration_us (project length after)}.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

ranges.description: Word ranges to delete: [{"from": 3, "to": 5}] (inclusive indices from transcript.get → words[].index). [3, 5] pairs and single indices are accepted too.

ripple_captions.description: Make caption cues follow the cut (later cues move left, removed words disappear from their cue). Default true.

segment_id.description: Clip whose words are deleted (from transcript.get → segments[].segment_id).

post.description:
Returns the transcript of the timeline — the Transcript panel: for every clip with sound (main track, overlays, audio tracks; or only segment_id) the recognised words mapped onto the TIMELINE (speed, speed curves, reverse and trims are honoured; words outside the clip's trimmed range are left out), with their source times and confidence, plus the clip's text. Clips whose material has not been transcribed are listed with transcribed=false (run transcript.transcribe). Word indices are per clip and are what transcript.delete_words expects; they change when the clip is edited, so re-read after edits. Clips that are not heard (muted track, volume 0 — e.g. a video whose sound was extracted to a linked audio clip) are omitted unless include_silent=true.
UI: Library/Transcript.

Cuts filler words out of the speech ("Remove filler words"): hesitation sounds that are always fillers — English um, uh, er, erm, ah, hmm, mm; Ukrainian/Russian е, еее, ем, ммм, а-а, хм, ну (elongated spellings like "ummm" match too) — and words often used as fillers only when they are set off by commas or sentence breaks: English like, you know, I mean, so, well, basically, actually, literally, kind of, sort of; Ukrainian типу, коротше, значить, ніби, як би, ну от, власне; Russian типа, короче, значит, как бы, вот, в общем. language=auto uses each transcript's language (all lists for other languages); words adds your own fillers (always removed). Each filler is cut like transcript.delete_words. Use preview=true to see the list first. One undo step.
UI: Library/Transcript/Remove filler words.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {found: [{segment_id, text, start_us, end_us}], count, removed_us, preview, cuts, captions_changed, duration_us}.

language.description: Built-in filler lists: auto (transcript language), all, none (only words), en, uk or ru.

preview.description: Only report what would be removed; the project is not changed.

words.description: Extra filler words or phrases to remove wherever they occur, e.g. ["okay", "right so"].

Cuts ripple like transcript.delete_words; captions follow. Use preview=true to see the pauses first. One undo step. (For silence detection from the audio level instead of words see ai.remove_silence.)
UI: Library/Transcript/Remove pauses.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {found: [{segment_id, start_us, end_us}], count, removed_us, preview, cuts, captions_changed, duration_us}.

Recognises the speech of one material (or of the materials of segment_ids, or of every audible clip when both are omitted) and stores it as the material's transcript: every word with its start/end in SOURCE time and a confidence. This is the Transcript panel's "Transcribe" button; no captions are created (use captions.auto or captions.from_transcript for that). Afterwards transcript.get shows the words on the timeline and transcript.delete_words / delete_text / remove_fillers / remove_pauses edit the video by editing the text. Materials that already have a transcript are skipped unless force=true or a different explicit language is requested. Runs as a background job like captions.auto (wait=true blocks). Not undoable (transcripts are analysis data; transcript.clear removes one).

post.description:
Puts the same transition between every pair of touching clips on a track (default: the main video track) — CapCut's "Apply to all" button. type/duration default to the transition of segment_id if given, else the first transition already on the track, else Mix 0.5 s. Each duration is clamped to half of the shorter clip of its pair; pairs with a gap or clips shorter than 0.2 s are skipped and counted. direction and softness work as in transition.set (they are applied on top of the copied type).
UI: Inspector/Transition/Apply to all.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {track_id, type, duration_us, applied: number of pairs set, skipped: number of pairs skipped}.

direction.description: Optional direction for transitions that have one (library item params.directions): the way the motion travels. For directional families (wipe_*, slide_*, push_*, cube_turn_*, whip_*) it selects the sibling id.

duration_us.description: Transition length; clamped per pair. See the description for the default. Unit: microseconds.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

segment_id.description: Copy type and duration from this clip's transition (the selected transition in the UI).

softness.description: Optional edge softness 0..1 (0 = hard edge, 1 = very soft) for mask transitions with params.softness=true (wipes, irises, shape reveals, checkerboard, luma/ink dissolves, burns, light sweep).

track_id.description: Track to process (main or overlay video track). Defaults to the main video track.

type.description: Transition id from library.list kind=transition. See the description for the default.

post.description:
Describes the transition that follows a clip — what the Transition inspector shows when a transition badge is selected: the stored type, its library id and name, duration, the current direction and softness (defaults filled in) and which options the transition supports, plus the longest duration the pair allows. has_transition=false (and no transition fields) when the cut is a hard cut. Change it with transition.set.
UI: Inspector/Transition.
Returns: {segment_id, has_transition, next_segment_id?, max_duration_us?, type?, id?, name?, duration_us?, direction?, softness?, options?}.

post.description:
Adds or replaces the transition between a clip and the NEXT clip on the same track (main or overlay video track), like dropping a transition between two clips in CapCut. The transition is stored on the left clip (segment.transition_out) and plays across the cut. The two clips must touch (the next clip starts where this one ends, within half a frame); otherwise a conflict error explains how to fix it. duration_us is clamped to half of the shorter of the two clips (the result reports clamped=true); both clips must be at least 0.2 s long. Optional direction (left/right/up/down) and softness (0..1) apply to transitions whose library item lists them in params (directions, softness); they are stored in the type as URL-style options, e.g. "bars_stagger?direction=up&softness=0.3" (directional families such as wipe_left + direction up store the sibling id "wipe_up"; values equal to the defaults are dropped). Strip everything from "?" to get the library id. Asking a transition for an option it does not have is an invalid_argument error listing its options.
UI: Library/Transitions.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {segment_id, next_segment_id, transition: {type, duration_us}, id, name, direction?, softness?, options: {directions, default_direction, softness, default_softness, direction_by_sibling}, clamped, max_duration_us}.

direction.description: Optional direction for transitions that have one (library item params.directions): the way the motion travels. For directional families (wipe_*, slide_*, push_*, cube_turn_*, whip_*) it selects the sibling id.

duration_us.description: Transition length (default 0.5 s). Clamped to half of the shorter neighbouring clip. Unit: microseconds.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

segment_id.description: ID of the target segment (clip). Get it from project.get → tracks[].segments[].id.

softness.description: Optional edge softness 0..1 (0 = hard edge, 1 = very soft) for mask transitions with params.softness=true (wipes, irises, shape reveals, checkerboard, luma/ink dissolves, burns, light sweep).

type.description: Transition id from library.list kind=transition, e.g. "mix", "black_fade", "wipe_left", "cube_turn_left", "iris_heart". A stored type with options ("blinds_h?direction=up") is accepted too.

post.description:
Reads a text segment aloud (CapCut's Text → Text to speech): speaks the segment's content with a local voice and places the speech as an audio clip starting exactly at the text's start, on the first free audio track. The text and the speech are linked (shared link_group) so they move together. Running it again on the same text REPLACES its previous speech (handy after editing the words or changing the voice). sync_duration=true is CapCut's "sync text and speech": the text segment is stretched or shortened to the length of the speech (never overlapping the next clip on its track — then clamped=true). Fails with invalid_argument for non-text or empty segments, conflict for locked tracks, not_available without a speech engine.
UI: Inspector/Text/Text to speech.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {segment_id (the new audio clip), track_id, material_id, start_us, duration_us, voice, provider, path, cached, text_segment_id, text_duration_us, synced, clamped, link_group, replaced_segment_ids[]}.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

rate.description: Speaking speed multiplier: 1 = the voice's normal speed, 0.5 = half as fast, 2 = twice as fast.

segment_id.description: ID of a text segment (on a text track) whose content is spoken. Get it from project.get or timeline.get.

sync_duration.description: When true, set the text segment's duration to the length of the speech.

voice.description: Voice to use: an id from tts.voices (e.g. "sapi:Microsoft Zira Desktop", "espeak:en-us"), a voice name, a language code ("en-US", "de", "ru" — picks a voice of that language) or part of a name ("zira"). Omit for the default voice (an English system voice when installed).

post.description:
Stores (or clears) the API key of an optional cloud speech provider so tts.voices / tts.speak / tts.from_text can use its voices next to the local engines. Supported provider: "elevenlabs" (natural multilingual voices; voice ids look like "elevenlabs:<voice_id>"). The key is saved only on this computer in the Kadr data folder (elevenlabs.key) — it is never returned by any command, never written to projects and only sent to the provider's own API. Text you synthesise is sent to the provider. The voice list is refreshed after saving and the result reports whether the key works.
Returns: {provider, stored: bool, working: bool, voices: count, error?} — the key itself is never echoed.

api_key.description: The provider API key (e.g. ElevenLabs keys start with "sk_"). Omit with clear=true to remove the stored key.

post.description:
Speaks text with a local voice and adds the speech to the timeline as a new audio clip (CapCut's Text to speech → Add to timeline). The speech is rendered by the selected engine (Windows SAPI, eSpeak NG or macOS say — see tts.voices), trimmed of leading/trailing silence, loudness-normalised to about -16 LUFS (peaks <= -1.5 dBTP, so voice-overs from every engine sound equally loud) and saved as a 48 kHz WAV in the project's cache (cache/tts/); the file is imported as a material named "Speech: <text>" and placed at at_us on the first free audio track (a new audio track when all are busy, or on track_id). The same text, voice and rate reuse the cached file. Up to 5000 characters per call; for narration split long scripts into sentences or paragraphs. Fails with not_available when no speech engine is installed (the hint explains what to install) and not_found for an unknown voice.
UI: Library/Audio/Text to speech.
Undoable with edit.undo.
Returns: {segment_id, track_id, material_id, start_us, duration_us, voice (voice id used), provider, path, cached}.

at_us.description: Timeline time where the speech starts (1 second = 1000000). Defaults to the playhead. Unit: microseconds.

project_id.description: ID of the project to operate on (e.g. "prj_8f3a..."). Get it from project.list or project.create.

rate.description: Speaking speed multiplier: 1 = the voice's normal speed, 0.5 = half as fast, 2 = twice as fast.

text.description: What to say (plain text, up to 5000 characters).

voice.description: Voice to use: an id from tts.voices (e.g. "sapi:Microsoft Zira Desktop", "espeak:en-us"), a voice name, a language code ("en-US", "de", "ru" — picks a voice of that language) or part of a name ("zira"). Omit for the default voice (an English system voice when installed).

post.description:
Lists the speech voices installed on this computer that tts.speak and tts.from_text can use, like the voice picker of CapCut's Text to speech (local engines send nothing online; the optional ElevenLabs cloud provider is used only after tts.set_api_key): Windows SAPI desktop voices (via PowerShell System.Speech, e.g. "Microsoft Zira Desktop"), eSpeak NG voices (~130 languages, robotic but universal) and macOS `say` voices. Each voice has an id "<provider>:<name>", a display name, a language code and a gender when known. providers[] tells which engines are available and why the others are not; default_voice is what is used when voice is omitted. The list is cached for 10 minutes; refresh=true re-detects (e.g. after installing a voice).
UI: Library/Audio/Text to speech.
Returns: {voices: [{id, provider, name, language, gender}], default_voice (voice id or "" when none), providers: [{id, name, available, voices, error}]}.

refresh.description: Re-detect engines and voices instead of using the cached list.
