post.description:
Asks GitHub whether a newer Kadr is published — Settings → Updates → "Check now" and Menu → "Check for updates…". Downloads latest.json (+ latest.json.sig) from the release repository (stable: the latest regular release; beta: the newest release including pre-releases, via the GitHub API), verifies its Ed25519 signature with the key built into Kadr and compares versions with semver rules (0.2.0-beta.1 < 0.2.0-rc.1 < 0.2.0). Nothing is downloaded or installed. available=true means a newer version exists; skipped=true means the user chose "Skip this version" for it (it is still reported here but never announced automatically); can_install=false (with reason) means this build cannot self-update — portable builds, development builds without a signing key, or a release without a Windows installer — so open release_url instead. A pre-release is never offered on the stable channel. Publishes update.available when a newer, not skipped version is found. Fails with not_available when GitHub cannot be reached, not_found when the repository has no release yet, and internal when the signature does not verify (the update is refused).
UI: Menu/Check for updates….
Returns: {current, latest, available, channel, prerelease, notes_markdown, notes_url, release_url, published_at, size (installer bytes), installer, signed, skipped, required (current is older than min_supported), min_supported, portable, can_install, reason, checked_at}.

channel.description: Release channel to look at: "stable" = regular releases only (the GitHub "latest" release), "beta" = also pre-releases such as 0.2.0-beta.1. Omit to use the channel saved in settings (update.settings).

post.description:
Downloads the installer of the newest version found by update.check (runs a check first when none was done in this session) into %TEMP%\Kadr-update\ and verifies its exact size and SHA-256 against the signed latest.json; a file that does not match is deleted and the update is refused. Runs in the background and returns immediately (state "downloading") unless wait=true; progress arrives as update.progress events, completion as update.ready, errors as update.failed. An installer already downloaded and verified is reused. Does not install anything — call update.install afterwards. Refused with not_available for portable builds, development builds without a signing key and releases without a Windows installer (open release_url instead), and with conflict when Kadr is already up to date.
UI: Settings/Updates/Download & install.
Returns: The update.status object (state downloading, ready or failed).

wait.description: Block until the download finished and was verified (can take minutes for ~100 MB) instead of returning at once.

post.description:
Installs the newest version and restarts Kadr — the "Download & install" button. Downloads and verifies the installer first if update.download has not finished (SHA-256 + size from the Ed25519-signed latest.json, checked again right before running), then starts it detached with /VERYSILENT /SUPPRESSMSGBOXES /NORESTART /CLOSEAPPLICATIONS /RELAUNCH and closes the desktop app about a second later. The installer upgrades in place, keeps all projects and settings, closes running Kadr processes (Kadr.exe, kadr-server.exe, kadr-mcp.exe) and starts Kadr again when done, so API clients lose their connection for a minute. UNSAVED WORK: projects are saved after every command, but running exports are cancelled. Requires confirm=true as a safety check. In the headless server nothing quits by itself: the result asks to exit. Refused for portable builds and builds without a signing key (not_available).
UI: Settings/Updates/Download & install.
Returns: {started, version, installer, args (the exact installer arguments), quitting (the app exits shortly), message}.

example1.summary: Install the downloaded update and restart

confirm.description: Must be true: confirms that Kadr may close (running exports stop) and the installer may run.

post.description:
Reads or changes the updater preferences stored in <data dir>/settings.json. Without arguments it only returns them. auto_check (default on) makes Kadr check GitHub in the background after startup, at most once every 24 hours, never blocking the editor; channel picks stable releases or also beta pre-releases. Builds that are themselves pre-releases (e.g. 0.1.0-beta.1) default to the beta channel. Changing the channel does not check by itself — call update.check afterwards.
UI: Settings/Updates.
Returns: {auto_check, channel, last_check (RFC 3339, omitted before the first check), skipped_version}.

auto_check.description: Check for updates automatically on startup (once a day). Omit to leave unchanged.

channel.description: "stable" (regular releases) or "beta" (also pre-releases). Omit to leave unchanged.

post.description:
Remembers a version as skipped — "Skip this version" under the release notes. A skipped version is no longer announced by the automatic startup check (no update.available event, no badge) but update.check still reports it with skipped=true, and any newer version is offered again normally. Only one version can be skipped; clear=true forgets it. Stored in settings.json.
UI: Settings/Updates/Skip this version.
Returns: The saved settings {auto_check, channel, last_check, skipped_version}.

clear.description: Forget the skipped version instead (version is ignored).

version.description: Version to skip, e.g. "0.2.0" (a leading v is accepted). Omit to skip the latest version found by update.check.

post.description:
Returns the updater state without contacting GitHub: state (idle | checking | up_to_date | available | downloading | ready | installing | failed), the result of the last check (latest, null before the first check), download progress, the verified installer path when ready, the last error, the saved settings, whether this is a portable build and whether this build carries an update signing key. Poll it every 1-2 s during update.download, or listen to the update.progress / update.ready / update.failed events instead.
UI: Settings/Updates.
Returns: {state, current, latest (update.check result or null), downloaded_bytes, total_bytes, progress 0..1, installer_path, error, settings{auto_check, channel, last_check, skipped_version}, portable, signing_key, repo, releases_url}.
Runs project commands in order on one project. If any call fails nothing is saved. All calls form a single undo step. With dry_run=true the result is computed and returned but not saved.
